Therefore, the accompanying verb must describe an event that has not yet occurred, such as V-る, V-ます, or V-てしまう, and cannot be in the past tense. The correct sentence (c) means: “The summer vacation is about to end.” For example: 「もうすぐ 電車が 来ますから、並んで待ってください。」 (The train will arrive soon, so please line up and wait.) Distinguish 「もうすぐ」 (soon, referring to the near future), 「すぐ（に）」 (immediately, referring to the very short interval between two consecutive actions, as in sentence a), and 「もう」 (already, used with the past). Thus, sentences ending in the past tense (~た / ~ました), as in b and d, can be eliminated.
